name: Shubham Jakhmola
title: AI Engineer
tagline: AI ENGINEER — AGENTS · RAG · DEEP LEARNING
pitch: I build LLM systems that ship — agents, retrieval pipelines, and the infrastructure behind them. This site rebuilds itself nightly from my repos; every glyph on screen is conserved matter, never created twice.
about: I'm an AI engineer focused on the practical end of the field — getting agents, retrieval systems, and neural networks to actually ship. I've built LLM agents that write and execute code, retrieval-augmented search over real document corpora, an automated support-ticketing system, and reinforcement-learning agents that play Super Mario. On the deep-learning side I've trained and compared U-Net, ResNet, and VGG architectures for medical image segmentation, and worked on behavioral-biometric identification. This site is itself a small example of how I like to work: it rebuilds itself nightly from my GitHub account via a scheduled pipeline, ranks my repos automatically, and summarizes them with an LLM — zero manual upkeep.

experience.title: Engineering foundations
experience.body: I started on the server side, building RESTful services on WildFly and the scraping pipelines that fed them. Most of it was unglamorous work: schema design, error paths, keeping a job alive when an upstream page changed shape overnight. Late in this stretch I wired OpenCV into a pipeline for the first time and hit a problem no query could answer. That was the turn. Everything after it is the same instinct pointed at models instead of endpoints.

experience.title: Deep learning research
experience.body: Research, properly: brain-tumor segmentation on BraTS 2020, training U-Net, ResNet and VGG against the same volumes so the comparison meant something. I learned more from the failures than from the architectures. Class imbalance on small tumour regions will hand you a metric that looks good and is mostly counting background. Alongside it I worked on behavioral-biometric identification, reaching 94.7% accuracy. The habit I took out of this period was measuring before believing, which is the only reason anything later shipped.

experience.title: Applied ML systems
experience.body: This was the period models had to leave the notebook. I trained reinforcement-learning agents to play Super Mario, ran sentiment analysis at a size where throughput mattered more than the last point of accuracy, and built speech-to-text bots that had to keep up with live audio. Serving turned out to be the hard half: batching, latency budgets, and what happens to a request while the model is still loading. FastAPI in front of everything.

experience.title: LLM agents & retrieval
experience.body: Now it is agents and retrieval. Autonomous coding agents that write and execute their own code, RAG search over real document corpora rather than a demo index, and automated ticket triage that has to be right often enough to be trusted with a queue. This site is part of the same work: it rebuilds itself nightly from the GitHub API, ranks the repos with a pure function, and writes its own summaries with an LLM. If a system needs me to remember to update it, I consider it unfinished.
